cells.blurb: Rian is expression-oriented and `:=` is single-assignment. A typed head is the type boundary; the body is the value.
cells.source:
# expression-oriented · := single assignment
def twice(n Int53) Int53 := n * 2
cells.title: The basics

cells.blurb: A sealed sum and clause-per-constructor dispatch. The same definition becomes a tagged match on the BEAM, an `enum` + `match` on Rust, a tag switch on JS, and a sealed `when` on Kotlin.
cells.source:
type Shape := Circle(radius Float64) | Square(side Float64)

def area(s val Shape) Float64
def area(Circle(r)) := 3.14159 * r * r
def area(Square(s)) := s * s
cells.title: Types & match

cells.blurb: Ordered clauses with a restricted guard sublanguage. The Maranget exhaustiveness gate proves the set total before any target is emitted — a missing case is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.

panes.ex:
def classify(n) when n < 0 do "negative" end
def classify(0) do "zero" end
def classify(n) do "positive" end

cells.source:
def classify(n Int53) String
def classify(n) when n < 0 := "negative"
def classify(0) := "zero"
def classify(n) := "positive"
cells.title: Clauses & guards

cells.blurb: A parameter's reference capability drives its Rust signature and its BEAM-side linearity — you never write a lifetime. `val` borrows (`&Shape`); `iso` owns and is consumed once (an owned `Shape`).
cells.source:
type Shape := Circle(radius Float64) | Square(side Float64)

def area(s val Shape) Float64
def area(Circle(r)) := 3.14159 * r * r
def area(Square(s)) := s * s

# `iso`: owned, consumed exactly once
def consume(s iso Shape) Float64 := area(s)
cells.title: Capabilities

cells.blurb: `case` is an expression that yields a value, proven total by the same exhaustiveness gate as clauses. It becomes a tagged match on the BEAM, an `enum` match on Rust, a tag switch on JS, and a labelled `run` on Kotlin.

panes.ex:
@type color :: :red | :green | :blue
def code(c) do case c do :red -> 1; :green -> 2; :blue -> 3 end end

cells.source:
type Color := Red | Green | Blue

def code(c val Color) Int53 := case c do
  Red -> 1
  Green -> 2
  Blue -> 3
end
cells.title: The `case` expression

cells.blurb: A `${expr}` hole stringifies by its statically-inferred type and lowers to a single-shot join (ADR-0069). `String` and `Int*` holes are byte-identical across every target — no hidden `Show` dispatch.

panes.ex: def greet(name, age) do <<"hi "::binary, name::binary, ", you are "::binary, Integer.to_string(age)::binary>> end

cells.source: def greet(name String, age Int53) String := "hi ${name}, you are ${age}"
